# Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga (Vb 17)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga* ("Analysis of Minor Items" or "Chapter on the Small Objects") is the seventeenth treatise of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Sarao and Long 2017; Kragh 2006; SuttaCentral]. Unlike the preceding doctrinal analyses of faculties, path factors, and enlightenment factors, this chapter serves as an analytical catalogue of unwholesome states, presenting extensive lists of mental defilements, vices, and evil qualities [Nyanatiloka 2007; Kragh 2006; Sujato 2012]. Following a *mātikā* (matrix), the exposition classifies these unwholesome dhammas numerically into groups of single items, pairs, triads, and up through sets of ten, supplemented by groupings of eighteen and 108 forms of craving [Nyanatiloka 2007; Ñāṇamoli 2010].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral connect sections of the text to several discourses on defilements, such as the *Cetokhila* suttas (MN 16; AN 5.205, AN 9.71, AN 10.14) and *Vinibandha* suttas (AN 5.206, AN 9.72, AN 9.82, AN 9.92), the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33), the *Dasuttara Sutta* (DN 34), and their Āgama counterparts (DĀ 10, MĀ 206, EĀ 51.4, T 1536.6), as well as related treatments in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (*Dukanikkhepa*, Ds 2.3.2), the *Niddesa*, and the *Puggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.2) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus matches confirm dense textual overlap with the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (Ds 2.3.2 and Ds 2.3.3), the *Brahmajāla Sutta* (DN 1), the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33), the *Dasuttara Sutta* (DN 34), and the numerical nipātas of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 4, AN 8, AN 10) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns passages with canonical and post-canonical Sanskrit works, including the Sarvāstivāda *Dharmaskandha*—which shares this category of defilements—as well as the *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, Vasubandhu's *Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇa*, and Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya* [DharmaNexus; Sujato 2012].
